# Theme architecture refactor plan

This document records the agreed architecture and invariants. Execution order, implementation targets, and acceptance gates are in the [phased implementation plan](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).

## Goals and invariants

- Split the current `@sabinmarcu/theme` implementation into a reusable theme core, a reusable family layer, and the concrete `@sabinmarcu/theme` implementation. Keep `@sabinmarcu/website-theme` as website-owned composition. Reuse and repair `@sabinmarcu/stylesheet` as the sole variable-token renderer; add optional devtools as a consumer, not a dependency of those theme layers.
- A theme is a stable public token view plus associated immutable descriptors describing source inputs, derived expressions, assignment scope, and serialization. Defining or extending a theme creates references and metadata without emitting CSS or accessing the DOM. The rendering harness emits initial CSS before first paint and updates source allocations later; components consume references without rendering values.
- Theme core and the concrete theme implementation know nothing about family construction, `base`, family selectors, or selection. Generator descriptors declare generic assignment scope (`shared` or `contextual`); core preserves this metadata, and family core consumes it to derive which properties receive per-family values. Family core depends on theme core and receives a theme as input.
- Retain functional setup/update calls and convenience contract returns, but use one stylesheet backend for build-time/static emission, SSR, and browser updates. Remove Vanilla Extract production, peer, and exported-type dependencies from theme core, family core, the concrete theme, and website-theme configuration. Keep Vanilla Extract in component/page styling consumers. Do not introduce a family-oriented `instantiate` method on a theme.
- Target the latest stable Chromium-based browsers and Safari's latest stable WebKit on macOS/iOS. Firefox compatibility is out of scope. Use stock shipping features, not nightly-only support or hidden experimental flags, and record the actual versions exercised. Native contrast, adaptive conditions, shadow rendering, and CSP behavior must work on both targeted engine families; a Chromium-only prototype is not cross-engine proof.
- Generators intrinsically declare immutable `kind: 'static' | 'variable'` metadata. Breakpoint generators always produce static output; palette/background and spacing generators always produce variable definitions. Theme composition consumes that classification, never decorates or reclassifies an existing generator. Independently, variable generators declare `scope: 'shared' | 'contextual'`; shared does not mean immutable, and light/dark remains a separate axis.
- Independently distinguish source variables from derived variables. A generator runs once per definition to establish token structure, source bindings, and CSS expressions; updates never rerun it or recompute derived values in JavaScript. Structural options stay fixed for that definition. Static generators evaluate their configured inputs once and do not participate in runtime updates. Derived variables have fixed formulas but changing effective values; they are not static tokens.
- Owned stylesheet contents are the single source of truth for live allocations. Application updates and devtools edits use the same update path; no independent mutable theme-value cache, devtools override layer, or value snapshot in the manifest competes with the sheet. Current serialization must reflect current contents, not construction-time CSS.
- Each family, including `base`, is an independent theme value set over the same public tokens. Resolve contextual values from that family's own inputs and defaults, never from another family member's values. `base` is not an inheritance parent. Shared-scope variables remain theme-wide by explicit descriptor policy, not because other families inherit them from `base`.
- A shared component imports the concrete theme's public tokens; an app may extend that same contract without changing the identity or names of the shared tokens. Extension must happen before a style module needs its static additions. Rendering must not be required to read tokens.
- Choose a validated CSS-variable prefix when creating/binding a contract; it is immutable for that contract. The default app namespace is `theme` (`--theme-*`); devtools uses `devtools-theme` (`--devtools-theme-*`). Namespace every owned source, derived, private family/variant, alias, dependency reference, and any property registration. Creating another namespace yields independent references/allocations from reusable definitions, never an in-place rename or re-prefixing extension.
- Build devtools as two packages: a framework-agnostic Web Components core and thin React components/bindings. Core owns shadow-DOM editors, handwritten structural CSS, manifest resolution, and the inspection/update interface. Keep ordinary TypeScript builds: embed CSS in TypeScript string modules rather than requiring a bundler, Vanilla Extract extraction, or unsupported raw CSS imports. Core initializes with a mount element and optional manifests; React forwards props and lifecycle. Use a private devtools UI theme without coupling to inspected app values. Chrome remains a future frontend.
- Manifests supplied to core initialization, or to the React component as props, are the primary access path. When the manifest argument/prop is omitted, devtools discovers designated embedded JSON manifests from HTML/DOM. Both paths use the same manifest schema and expose only declared root allocations; absent data exposes no editable theme. Neither path requires page theme runtime setup or a window registry.
- Allocate sources at each harness's designated root. Devtools inspects only manifest-declared application root allocations in owned light-DOM stylesheets, including all standard/family members. It never inspects its private UI theme or sheets inside Web Component shadow roots, whether open or closed. Programmatic manifests do not widen that scope. No arbitrary element overrides, DOM picker, or local token writes. Renderer shadow support exists for private UI rendering, not for shadow-tree inspection.

## Target package boundaries

| Package | Owns | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@sabinmarcu/theme-core` (proposed) | Vanilla-Extract-free contract allocation with immutable construction-time prefixes, descriptors, one-time compilation, source codecs, extension, generic variable/expression namespacing, and setup/update over the shared renderer | Stylesheet document/shadow backend and utilities; no concrete theme, family, Vanilla Extract, or mandatory React import |
| `@sabinmarcu/theme-family` (proposed) | Family construction, interpretation of descriptor scope, independent family defaults, root allocations, family/variant mapping and selection, and family inspection metadata | `@sabinmarcu/theme-core`; never the concrete implementation or Vanilla Extract |
| `@sabinmarcu/theme` | Concrete shared schema, CSS formula choices, source defaults/scopes, stable public token references, and typed direct setup/update exports | `@sabinmarcu/theme-core`; never family core or Vanilla Extract |
| `@sabinmarcu/website-theme` | Website family names and independent values/defaults, shared values, and website-specific static extension including viewport breakpoints | `@sabinmarcu/theme`, `@sabinmarcu/theme-family`, and core utilities; no Vanilla Extract dependency |
| `@sabinmarcu/stylesheet` | Owned current rules, server serialization, document/shadow-root attachment and update, snapshots/notifications, and optional embedding helpers; no concrete schema | Platform APIs/utilities; explicit CSS-root/allocation context, with React/SSR wrappers optional rather than core imports |
| `@sabinmarcu/theme-devtools-core` (proposed) | Web Components and shadow-root UI, handwritten embedded CSS, private namespaced UI theme, manifest resolution, root source inspection/update, subscriptions, and live export | Theme core/stylesheet interfaces and browser APIs; no React, Chrome, inspected-schema, Vanilla Extract, or bundler dependency. Build with ordinary TypeScript |
| `@sabinmarcu/theme-devtools-react` (proposed) | React component hosting the core, manifest props, lifecycle integration, and React bindings to its interface; no second editor/state implementation | React and `@sabinmarcu/theme-devtools-core`; no reverse dependency from devtools core or theme layers |
| `apps/website` | Initial stylesheet emission through its server/build harness, optional manifest embedding, and runtime family/variant selection | Website theme and appropriate stylesheet/SSR helpers; Vanilla Extract remains for component/page styles |

Avoid giving the concrete implementation an implicit dependency on the family package through a re-export or runtime import. Keep Storybook as a consumer of the family API, not its owner.

Public variable contracts must remain plain nested `var(--...)` reference trees with precise literal/template types. Keep descriptors and editor metadata outside that tree. Static additions remain available in the public token view but are omitted from the variable-only contract projection required by whole-contract assignment helpers. Vanilla Extract compatibility is structural, not a runtime brand or registration dependency.

## API sketch (illustrative, not a final signature)

```ts
// @sabinmarcu/theme: shared, single-identity contract in the default 'theme' namespace.
export const theme = defineTheme({
  colors: {
    primary: paletteGenerator(),
    secondary: paletteGenerator(),
    info: paletteGenerator(),
    success: paletteGenerator(),
    warning: paletteGenerator(),
    error: paletteGenerator(),
    background: backgroundGenerator(),
  },
  grid: gridGenerator(),
});
export const setupTheme = createThemeSetup(theme);

// @sabinmarcu/website-theme: exported for website styles needing app tokens.
export const websiteTheme = extendTheme(theme, {
  breakpoint: breakpointGenerator([
    ['mobile', 700],
    ['tablet', 1000],
  ]),
});

// @sabinmarcu/website-theme: family-specific composition, not theme implementation.
export const setupThemeFamily = createThemeFamily(websiteTheme, {
  families: ['personal', 'projects', 'articles'],
});

// App server/build harness: setup populates the owned sheet, not a .css.ts emitter.
const renderedWebsiteTheme = setupThemeFamily(themeValues); // Same websiteTheme contract.
// The harness emits that stylesheet before first paint; manifest embedding is optional.

// A direct, non-family app can instead call setupTheme(values), returning theme.
```

Assignment scope is authoritative descriptor policy, not merely eligibility for an app-owned `vary` list. Family construction derives contextual properties from the descriptors, including those introduced by extensions. Static descriptors have no assignment-scope choice and never receive per-family contracts. Apps choose family names, values, and selection, not which properties vary.

The family call remains functional. It allocates shared source variables once at the harness root and independently allocates contextual source variables plus namespaced derived expressions for every family, including `base`. Inputs and defaults are local to each family. A `pick` operation maps public source and derived references to the selected family's root-allocated variables; it never replaces the token object imported by components. Scoped family selectors change only that mapping, not source allocations. Map the complete variable subtree rather than changing a public source and expecting inherited derived custom properties to rebind. Light/dark remains a separate variant axis for direct and family themes.

## Family setup and update input layout

- Use explicit `shared` and `families` containers for family setup, family updates, and devtools live export. Each subtree follows the theme's nested source-input paths, not its generated token-output shape. Descriptor scope determines legal fields; callers cannot make a contextual source shared by placing it in the other container.
- `shared` contains shared-scope sources allocated once outside all family members. `families` maps every member, including ordinary `base`, to contextual source inputs with independent local defaults. This avoids configuration/family-name collisions and does not add cross-family inheritance.
- Setup resolves missing fields from the relevant local defaults and rejects unresolved required inputs. Updates may omit either container, members, or supported nested paths/variants; omitted allocations retain their current values. Static/derived tokens are excluded, shared fields are invalid within any family, and contextual fields are invalid within `shared`, including mixed-scope theme branches.
- Direct non-family setup remains the unwrapped nested source-input shape. Manifest input paths and family live exports include the appropriate `shared` or `families.<member>` addressing; source values still come from the authoritative sheet, not manifest snapshots.

Example for a reduced schema with shared `grid` and contextual `colors.primary`:

```ts
setupThemeFamily({
  shared: { grid: 16 },
  families: {
    base: { colors: { primary: '#0cf' } },
    personal: { colors: { primary: '#f0c' } },
    projects: { colors: { primary: '#3c8' } },
  },
});
```

The website-owned package may continue to export `themeColors` or rename it to `themeValues`; either way, breakpoint inputs leave variable setup values. Static breakpoint queries are computed by the website extension before a `.css.ts` rule reads them. The app harness must emit the owned stylesheet for variable values to exist, including SSR pages without theme runtime setup; neither static output nor public references depend on that emission. Component/page styles remain authored with Vanilla Extract and consume our tokens.

## Contract namespaces and allocation roots

- Configure a bare prefix such as `theme` or `devtools-theme` at contract creation; the allocator forms valid `--prefix-*` names and detects collisions. Preserve current public app variable names in the default namespace. Retire or migrate unprefixed private allocations rather than leaving hidden shared inputs between namespaces.
- Bind reusable compiled symbolic definitions to independent reference trees. A new namespace does not mutate the original contract, borrow its allocated values, or rerun value generators. All derived dependencies, private family/variant names, mappings, and manifest bindings must refer to the new namespace. Do not rewrite arbitrary source-value strings or promise that deliberately supplied external CSS references become isolated automatically.
- Extension inherits the base namespace and preserves existing names/identity. Namespace selection is not an extension option or a runtime value patch. Static output is unaffected by variable naming. Namespacing metadata stays outside the plain variable-reference tree.
- Components importing the default concrete token view remain bound to `--theme-*`. Consumers of a custom namespace must author styles against its matching view; do not add app/devtools alias bridges that obscure this dependency. Devtools may reuse schema/generator definitions but uses its own bound UI view, independent defaults, and appropriate units.
- Namespace and allocation root are separate identities. The same prefix can be reused safely in independent host/document roots with separate mutable sheets. Detect conflicting ownership of the same allocations within one root; qualify private rendering/family identities so independent configurations do not collide. CSS prefixes do not isolate custom-element registry names or external styling of a host.
- The renderer receives an explicit CSS-root and allocation target: document-root rules normally use `:root`, while a stylesheet inside a component shadow root allocates on `:host`. The UI mount container, private UI-theme host, and manifest-declared inspected root are not interchangeable. Preserve source/formula co-location and inheritance; an inherited derived formula does not rebind to a descendant input override.

Illustrative construction options, not final helper signatures:

```ts
const appTheme = defineTheme(sharedDefinition, { prefix: 'theme' });
const devtoolsTheme = defineTheme(devtoolsDefinition, { prefix: 'devtools-theme' });
```

## Generator and live-value model

- Compile variable generators against symbolic source references and fixed structural configuration, not a sample value that determines runtime output. Keep source bindings and derived dependency references explicit so generic namespacing can bind them without rerunning the generator or rewriting arbitrary strings with regex.
- Each generator factory carries its own output kind into the descriptor it creates: breakpoints are static, palette/background/grid definitions are variable. Factories take structural/static configuration and optional source defaults, not setup-time allocations. Core composition derives references/static output and setup/update types from the generator's discriminant; neither output value types nor property names determine classification. There are no consumer-side static/variable decorators or reclassification escape hatches.
- A palette source is its main color; muted/emphasis and other outputs use CSS expressions such as `oklch(from var(--source) l calc(c * 0.5) h)`. Grid sources drive `calc(...)` expressions with fixed coefficients. Updating sources changes browser-computed values without regenerating formulas.
- Fibonacci spacing uses fixed ratios `2, 3, 5, 8, ...`: `m` is the base source, and each small/large pair is `base / ratio` and `base * ratio`. Thus `s/l` use 2, `xs/xl` use 3, and `xxs/xxl` use 5; larger structural scales continue the sequence. Ratios are compiled once into CSS expressions, and all values scale with the source and remain positive for a positive base. This intentionally replaces legacy Fibonacci offsets; the default eight-point scale is unchanged.
- Source codecs map nested setup inputs to declarations and back to setup-compatible live values. Prefer directly readable source representations, such as a unitless numeric allocation when the input is numeric; otherwise declare the unit/conversion codec explicitly. Do not recover inputs by inverting derived colors or spacing values.
- Derive palette contrast and background text with browser-native `contrast-color()`; accept its browser-defined algorithm and white-on-tie behavior rather than pinning the former JavaScript WCAG rule. Retain input-dependent background mix percentages: surface 10%/20%, elevated 20%/40%, and raised 30%/50% toward text for light/dark polarity; depressed 20% and recessed 30% toward the opposite color. Polarity follows the derived foreground, not the selected light/dark variant. Implement those branches in CSS with verified computed-value conditions and a declared feature floor; do not replace them with fixed weights, freeze initial choices, or rerun generators.
- All source and derived family allocations belong to the harness root. CSS custom properties containing formulas resolve dependencies where declared; inherited formulas do not automatically rebind when a descendant changes a source. Descendants may select the complete root-allocated family/variant mapping but do not allocate source overrides.

## Phase 1: Inventory and lock down behavior

1. Record the public import paths in `@sabinmarcu/theme`, `@sabinmarcu/website-theme`, the website, and Storybook. Capture the shape of `theme`, family selectors, updater inputs, generated CSS variable names, and CSS layer ordering. Treat `theme`, `family`, `ssr`, `runtime`, and `family.runtime` exports as migration surfaces.
2. Characterize palette/background structure, existing light/dark/selection behavior, grid, and mappings. Verify the chosen native contrast policy without pinning the old JavaScript algorithm or incidental color serialization. Assert adaptive mix percentages for light/dark input polarity, and prove source edits can flip foreground and branch while preserving variant selection semantics. Cover independent defaults, root isolation, partial/scalar-to-variant patches, and complete replacement where patching is unsupported. Use emitted declarations and actual browser-computed values, not token references alone.
3. Cover static exact breakpoint boundaries and ordered-definition rejection, plus the selected multiplicative Fibonacci scale: every pair responds to base changes, fourth/larger pairs have positive coefficients, and the default eight-point output is unchanged. Cover preservation of stylesheet rules, caller patches, SSR values, ownership, and nonces; complete namespace/dependency isolation, default public names, host/document contexts, and independent app/devtools/same-prefix hosts.
4. Add compile-time assertions for generator-owned immutable output kinds, setup/update inputs derived only from variable descriptors, precise static output types, construction namespaces, stable extension, supported patches, contextual family fields, and exact breakpoint outputs/keys. Verify independent contracts in a Vanilla Extract consumer fixture with style/assignment/fallback helpers and invalid-shape cases; keep that tooling outside production dependencies and replace current `any`/`@ts-ignore` paths.

**Exit:** Tests and type assertions characterize current intentional behavior and separately expose confirmed defects. The existing website and Storybook still work.

## Phase 2: Establish the dependency-free core and unified stylesheet backend

1. Introduce generator-owned descriptors with immutable `kind: 'static' | 'variable'`, public/static output types, typed source/default inputs, codecs, and derived dependencies. Variable generators also own `scope: 'shared' | 'contextual'` and source/derived roles. Breakpoint factories always create static descriptors; palette/background/grid factories create variable descriptors. Theme definition and extension consume these directly, without classification wrappers, name/type inference, or caller overrides. Typed authoring helpers may define a generator's intrinsic metadata, not relabel an already-defined generator. Replace positional tuples and compile each definition once.
2. Own a contract allocator with validated immutable construction-time prefixes, deterministic valid names, collision checks, and precise `var(--...)` types. Default `theme` preserves public app names; nondefault prefixes create fresh independent views. Namespace all allocations, including private family/variant variables, aliases, expressions, and any registrations. Keep namespace/descriptors outside the variable tree and static output outside whole-contract variable projections. Do not import Vanilla Extract or its types, mutate a live prefix, or silently retain unprefixed private inputs.
3. Make setup/update inputs follow nested descriptor paths (`colors.primary`, `grid`), with static descriptors excluded. Setup resolves complete inputs from the target's own defaults and supplied values. Updates patch current source allocations read through the owned sheet and codecs, never a competing normalized-input cache. Support partial theme grouping and light/dark patches; scalar shorthand writes both variants. Other generator inputs are complete replacements unless their descriptor explicitly supports patches.
4. Bind compiled symbolic source/derived graphs to a chosen namespace without rerunning generators. Keep this generic primitive free of family names/selectors/layers. Rebind dependency references structurally, not by regex string replacement; static output is unchanged. Distinguish namespace from root/rendering ownership and detect conflicting allocations within a root while allowing independent hosts to reuse a prefix.
5. Repair the unified stylesheet backend with explicit document or shadow CSS-root/allocation context, not hard-coded global `document`/`head` behavior. Server/build emission precedes first paint; browser attachment adopts current values. Use `:root` for document allocations and `:host` for host allocations through an inner shadow sheet. Patch via CSSOM and synchronize current serialization, preserving rules, layers, caller inputs, nonces, ownership, and isolated SSR state. Reacquire handles after text replacement. Shared immutable structural UI sheets are separate from per-harness mutable theme sheets. React wrappers never overwrite owned live contents.
6. Share this renderer and update contract between static/SSR and runtime delivery; retire `createGlobalTheme` rendering and `assignInlineVars` conversion from theme internals. Preserve observable stylesheet identity and Storybook synchronization where compatible, migrating consumers directly where needed. Normal rendering and updates must work with no inspection manifest.
7. Prove definition/extension is DOM-free and emits no values, namespace binding preserves original references without generator reruns, and source updates leave formulas fixed. Exercise two prefixes from reusable definitions, complete private/dependency isolation, default name compatibility, document/shadow inheritance, independent hosts, SSR adoption/current snapshots, and request/render isolation. Browser-computed derived values and consumer type/build checks provide evidence; no repeated color parsing or derived computation belongs in updates.

**Exit:** Core defines and renders a direct theme through one stylesheet backend without importing concrete, family, React UI, or Vanilla Extract code. CSS computes derived values; owned current contents support reads, updates, and current serialization.

## Phase 3: Add extension without implicit rendering

1. Implement `extendTheme(base, additions)` as pure composition inheriting the base namespace. Preserve existing nested reference identity and public variable names, and add paths without regenerating the base. A different namespace requires a separately constructed/bound contract, never an extension override or live rename.
2. Reject path collisions by default. An explicit replacement API can be considered separately, but silent overrides must not change tokens already imported by shared components.
3. Permit static additions (computed once at definition) and variable additions with their own source bindings, defaults, codecs, and precompiled formulas. Preserve static output types, such as exact media-query strings, and exclude static output from setup/update inputs. Extension must not rerun base generators or change their references.
4. Carry descriptor metadata through extension so direct setup and family core see the same complete shape. Keep the public token view and the descriptor associated. Setup calls return the existing contract being rendered as a convenience, including an extended contract when supplied; they must never create a new contract, extend it, or change its identity during rendering. Family setup returns the public contract, not a selected family's namespaced contract.
5. Test independent extensions and namespace bindings separately: same-namespace base identity, unchanged original contracts after creating another prefix, static access before rendering, added source inputs, variable-only projections, and no generator execution during binding/rendering/updates.

**Exit:** Components using base tokens and app styles using extended tokens can coexist without import-order initialization.

## Phase 4: Extract theme family core

1. Implement `createThemeFamily(theme, { families })` against immutable namespaced descriptors, with no `vary` list or concrete factory dependency. Bind contextual source/derived contracts and expressions beneath the theme's chosen prefix using generic namespacing, without rerunning generators. Qualify independent rendering/configuration identities so private family/variant allocations cannot collide, and never escape into another namespace.
2. Use family inputs shaped as `{ shared: SharedInputs, families: FamilyInputs }`, preserving nested source paths within each container. Allocate shared sources/formulas once at the root, outside every member; allocate contextual sources/formulas independently for `base` and named families. Derive both input types from descriptor scope, rejecting shared/static/derived fields in family payloads and contextual fields in `shared`. Prune mixed-scope branches per descriptor rather than classifying whole branches. Direct setup has no family wrappers.
3. Replace base-plus-override inheritance with local defaults and independent family values. Missing contextual inputs resolve from that family's own defaults/configuration, never another member. Apply the agreed partial patches to current owned source allocations and preserve omitted variants/paths. Assert contextual isolation and deliberate shared-input effects. Reject unknown families and duplicate/reserved `base` names; built-in `base` is an ordinary member, not a defaults provider.
4. Map the complete public contextual variable tree to selected root-allocated family values at the default selector and `data-theme-family` scopes. Preserve `pick`, `families`, `selectors`, `themes` where needed, and existing `data-theme-variant`/`light-dark(...)` behavior. Descendant scopes select mappings only; they do not allocate source values. Test family and variant selection together, including inactive members' root allocations.
5. Move family setup/update/pick wrappers and family manifest projection to family core, delegating all declarations to the shared stylesheet backend. Core and the concrete implementation must not acquire a family dependency. Family setup returns the existing public theme contract, not private family references.

**Exit:** A small synthetic theme with different token paths works with family core, proving there is no hidden dependency on the concrete schema.

## Phase 5: Recompose the concrete theme and website

1. Declare the concrete shared schema and default `theme` namespace, preserving public color/grid paths and names while replacing value-dependent generators. Expose reusable definitions where needed for independently prefixed consumers without coupling them to app-bound references or values. Remove family and Vanilla Extract dependencies; migrate legacy private variables under the owning namespace and keep story-only styling out of production entries. Devtools binds its own UI definition/view under `devtools-theme`, not an extension that renames the app theme.
2. Configure ordered viewport breakpoint definitions in `@sabinmarcu/website-theme` with the core's static generator and extend the shared view before constructing families. Migrate website breakpoint readers to that extended view and object definitions to ordered tuples. Keep all theme configuration independent of Vanilla Extract and avoid workspace-to-app dependencies.
3. Keep values in website-owned configuration; remove breakpoint inputs from variable setup and declare colors contextual/grid shared in their descriptors. Materialize formerly inherited family values into each family's own inputs/defaults to preserve the website's appearance without inheritance. Move theme value emission out of the Vanilla Extract `theme.css.ts` boundary into the app's server/build harness using the shared stylesheet backend. Emit source values and formulas before first paint, retain client selection without reinitializing values, and optionally embed the generated JSON manifest. Component/page `.css.ts` files remain Vanilla Extract consumers of token references and static queries.
4. Migrate Storybook's demo and website families to independent defaults and the same stylesheet setup/update path. Remove breakpoint inputs and use explicit story/app breakpoint definitions. Ensure preview/manager mirroring reads current sheet contents and theme overrider references remain stable. Retain Vanilla Extract in styling consumers, not the theme layers.
5. If motion tokens/transitions are added, do so after the split as a separate feature: shared duration/easing variable contracts in the concrete theme; a pure transition-string helper in core or the implementation; runtime changes to variable values should not require regenerating CSS rules.

**Exit:** Direct and family consumers share one rendering backend; the website has correct initial CSS without theme runtime setup, extended static queries remain authorable without rendering, and Storybook observes current runtime contents. Theme layers have no Vanilla Extract dependency; component/page styling still uses it.

## Phase 6: Migrate exports, validate, and complete the clean cutover

1. Migrate all consumers of old subpath imports (`theme`, `family`, `ssr`, `runtime`, `family.runtime`) to the appropriate package owners, retaining only entry points that belong to the new API. Add the required package dependencies directly rather than forwarding family APIs through the concrete theme. Publish a migration table and remove obsolete exports in the same cutover; do not introduce compatibility aliases, forwarding re-exports, or legacy input adapters.
2. Update Yarn dependencies and Moon edges in dependency order: stylesheet backend, theme core, family core, concrete theme, website theme, website/Storybook, devtools core, then React bindings. Remove Vanilla Extract dependencies from theme layers and devtools; retain it only in actual component/page/Storybook styling consumers. Devtools CSS is embedded in TypeScript modules, so its build needs no extraction plugin or bundler. Follow generated TypeScript project-reference conventions and do not edit `dist` outputs.
3. Run applicable builds/type and behavior checks, source-file ESLint fixes (not Markdown), and the website build. Build a representative Vanilla Extract consumer against independent contracts. Browser-smoke the latest stable Chromium and Safari/WebKit, recording versions: initial SSR paint without theme runtime setup, root updates, native contrast/adaptive branch changes, light/dark/family selection, scoped mapping, and Storybook synchronization. Firefox is not a verification target.
4. Inspect static/SSR and current runtime CSS for stable default public names, complete per-prefix private/source/derived/dependency ownership, fixed formulas, shared/family allocations, mappings/variants, and exact breakpoints. Verify app/devtools and same-prefix independent-host isolation, appropriate document/host selectors, current serialization, no generator reruns/SSR resets, and no rendering dependency on manifests.
5. Remove obsolete implementation code, exports, and migration-only scaffolding as consumers move to the new API. Document the breaking cutover and publish concise guidance for direct theme setup, app extension, independent family setup/defaults, and when static inputs must be configured. No compatibility adapters remain or are introduced as part of the migration.

**Exit:** No dependency cycle, concrete/core-to-family import, Vanilla Extract dependency in theme layers, static updater, runtime generator execution, competing mutable value store, or legacy compatibility path. Existing references/names and intentional variant behavior are preserved; every removed entry point has a documented replacement and all consumers use the new API.

## Unified stylesheet design and verified constraints

- Keep identifiable SSR `<style>` output and browser adoption, but replace the current regex-based updater. One backend serializes server/build rules and updates owned browser declarations. Static asset and SSR element emission are delivery choices, not separate theme renderers. This replaces the website's current Vanilla Extract theme-value emission, not its component/page styling.
- The sheet's current allocations are authoritative. Use CSSOM as the browser's parsing/update mechanism and synchronize serialized style contents after commits; do not leave initial DOM text behind while maintaining a separate live CSSOM state. Read live sources through descriptors/codecs, preserve unrelated rules, and expose current snapshots rather than frozen initial `.raw` output. Application and devtools patches use this same path.
- Actual-source browser smoke runs verified simple SSR adoption/source updates and exposed descendant-selector rule loss, caller-array consumption, inconsistent duplicate-ID updates, and missing mount nonces. These are required regression boundaries for the new updater.
- CSSOM-only edits preserve rules but do not change `innerHTML`; the current Storybook mirror polls/copies that text. Synchronizing current contents preserves this integration contract. If snapshot/event-based mirroring replaces polling, migrate it in the clean cutover and verify preview/manager behavior. Text replacement invalidates cached CSSOM handles and reparses the owned sheet; commit related changes together and measure this bounded token-sheet path before adding a competing cache.
- Token descriptors own semantics; optional manifests project rendered root bindings, source/editor kinds, codecs, families/variants, and read-only output, not mutable values. No manifest means no devtools access; normal rendering/update remains unaffected. Embedding is safe and inert. Devtools uses handwritten shadow CSS and its own namespaced theme through the same renderer, not a separate token-value engine or Vanilla Extract stylesheet build.
- Compatibility proof during planning used CSS 1.21.2, dynamic 2.1.5, and TypeScript 6.0.2. Independently built reference trees matched `createGlobalThemeContract` output, worked with actual assignment/fallback helpers in Chromium, and type-checked with `style` and helpers with zero diagnostics plus negative reference/shape assertions. Published types are structural `var(--${string})` trees, not nominal brands: [CSS declarations](https://unpkg.com/@vanilla-extract/css@1.21.2/dist/vanilla-extract-css.cjs.d.ts), [dynamic declarations](https://unpkg.com/@vanilla-extract/dynamic@2.1.5/dist/vanilla-extract-dynamic.cjs.d.ts). Preserve this compatibility through consumer checks without production dependencies.

## Devtools Web Components and shadow ownership

- Author structural CSS in TypeScript template-string modules and embed it in component shadow roots. Ordinary `tsc` does not embed standalone `.css` imports; no bundler/extraction pipeline is part of the devtools build. React hosts/interfaces with these components rather than maintaining another UI.
- Allocate the private UI theme at the outer devtools host through the shared renderer, with independent defaults and `devtools-theme` names. Its inner shadow sheet targets `:host`; sources and formulas are co-located so widgets inherit without local overrides. These UI allocations are never devtools inspection targets, even if metadata names them. Inspected application roots and their owned light-DOM sheets remain separate.
- Custom properties cross host/shadow boundaries by inheritance; any property registrations we introduce must retain that intended inheritance. App properties may still be present inside the shadow tree, but UI styles consume only the devtools-bound token view and do not fall back to the app's namespace. Reuse definitions where appropriate, not the app's already-bound references.
- Shadow DOM isolates descendant selectors, not all inheritance or host/ancestor layout. Explicitly set UI typography, control colors, and color-scheme. `rem` still refers to the document root font size inside a shadow tree; choose UI spacing representations independent of app-controlled root fonts, such as fixed lengths or a deliberate host-font-relative basis. Namespace separation prevents accidental variable collisions, not hostile styling of the host or deliberate external CSS references in source values.
- Immutable structural CSS sheets may be shared per component type, namespace, and owner document through `adoptedStyleSheets` where supported; do not parse identical CSS separately for every widget unnecessarily. Mutable theme-allocation sheets belong to individual harnesses/hosts and must never be shared across independent devtools instances. A `<style>` fallback must honor CSP/nonce requirements; shadow roots do not bypass the page's policy. Keep current theme serialization authoritative regardless of structural CSS delivery.
- Namespace custom-element tag names as well as variables. Defer `HTMLElement` subclass creation and registration until browser initialization; imports must remain SSR-safe. Register against the mount element's document/realm, with idempotent registration and an explicit policy for incompatible package versions. Dispose owned hosts/UI sheets/subscriptions, never inspected application allocations or edits.
- Inspection and manifest DOM discovery are light-DOM-only. Do not traverse open/closed shadow roots, inspect private devtools sheets, or add a closed-root inspection connection. Resolve declared application allocation roots and their owned light-DOM sheets; metadata does not authorize inaccessible or out-of-scope targets. General renderer support for shadow roots remains necessary for the private UI but does not expand devtools access. A future Chrome transport targets this same application scope, not hidden component internals.

## Devtools initialization and manifest delivery

- Core initialization receives a UI mount element and optional manifests. React renders a container and forwards props; core creates/hosts its Web Components and a private UI-theme allocation host inside that container. The container, private UI allocation host, and inspected app allocation roots have distinct ownership. Inspected root bindings come from manifest records.
- Programmatic manifests are authoritative when provided. DOM discovery is a fallback, not an implicit union with supplied manifests. This lets an application expose a deliberate subset of themes even if the page contains other embedded catalogs.
- Recommended exact omission semantics: `undefined` means discover manifests from designated inert JSON blocks in the inspection document; an explicit empty list means expose no themes and do not fall back. Invalid provided manifests are reported/validated, not treated as permission to discover unrelated DOM entries. Default DOM discovery uses the mount element's owner document, not only its subtree. Keep the inspection connection concept separate from UI mounting for a future Chrome panel in another document/context.
- Both manifest paths share validation, codecs, root-only editing, and live export, with targets restricted to owned application allocations in light-DOM sheets. Explicit data cannot authorize shadow/private UI inspection. Discovery never executes contents, guesses schemas from CSS, or reads hidden React/window state. Programmatic delivery does not automatically emit HTML; optional light-DOM embedding supports independent discovery and a future Chrome frontend.
- The core interface supports manifest replacement and disposal. React forwards changed props without recreating inspected theme allocations. Disposal removes owned Web Components, private UI allocations, and subscriptions, but leaves inspected light-DOM source values and metadata unchanged. DOM refresh policy remains to be settled and must not turn explicit catalogs into a merged discovery result.

Illustrative API, not final exported names:

```tsx
const devtools = createThemeDevtools(container, { manifests });
devtools.setManifests(nextManifests);
devtools.destroy();

<ThemeDevtools manifests={manifests} />
```

## Phase 7: Build the devtools core and React bindings

1. Finalize manifest/editor schemas, source codecs, namespaces, and shadow-root rendering context alongside Phase 2. Implement devtools-core Web Components with handwritten CSS embedded in TypeScript string modules and ordinary `tsc` builds; no Vanilla Extract extraction or bundler. Defer element class creation/registration and DOM work until initialization so imports remain SSR-safe. Use private UI defaults/root allocations and the `devtools-theme` namespace; styles consume that bound view, not inspected app tokens. React hosts/binds to this same implementation, forwards manifests, and manages lifecycle without duplicate editor logic or applied state. Public helper names remain implementation details.
2. Build one JSON-safe schema from theme/family descriptors and owned light-DOM application root bindings. Programmatic manifests/React props are primary; only omitted input triggers light-DOM embedded-data discovery. Validate both paths identically, without implicit merging, CSS inference, shadow traversal, or private UI access. Include allocated family members/variants, codecs, and read-only outputs, not live snapshots. SSR embedding is optional; no metadata means no access.
3. Read live application-root sources from declared owned light-DOM sheets and patch through the normal update path. Preserve partial/local-default semantics and shared effects; export direct nested inputs or family `{ shared, families }` values. No element/derived overrides or applied-value cache. Private devtools and shadow-root sheets remain excluded even if supplied metadata names them. Reject/report invalid ownership/scope rather than reading guesses or creating overrides. UI disposal preserves inspected application allocations.
4. Verify plain TypeScript-built Web Components/React bindings in latest stable Chromium and Safari/WebKit. Test private UI shadow inheritance/namespace isolation separately from application inspection: only declared light-DOM sheets/root allocations are editable; open/closed component and devtools sheets are ignored/rejected, including programmatic entries. Cover families/variants, shared/partial edits, current serialization/export, native contrast/adaptive markers, SSR/adoption, lifecycle/realms, resets/fonts, CSP/nonces, and manifest precedence. No consumer bundler is required; missing metadata does not impair rendering; Firefox is outside scope.

**Exit:** Plain TypeScript-built devtools core renders its private namespaced Web Components UI, with React hosting the same implementation. Inspection/editing is limited to manifest-enabled application root allocations in owned light-DOM sheets. Shadow-root and private UI sheets are never inspection targets; renderer shadow support is only a separate rendering capability. Source-only edits/live export use the shared authoritative backend, preserve family/instance isolation, and survive UI disposal. Chrome remains a future frontend for this same scope.

## Settled decisions

- **Nested setup/update inputs:** Value-input paths follow contract grouping (`colors.primary`, `grid`) instead of flattening generator names at the root. Generator inputs remain seed values or their existing structured inputs; callers do not supply every generated token. Static descriptors are excluded. Migrate existing flat-input callers; this changes input addressing, not public token references or CSS variable names.
- **Preserve existing light/dark behavior:** Retain the current `light-dark(...)` output and `data-theme-variant` selector behavior across build-time and runtime rendering, including their interaction with family selection. Capture the existing behavior in executable contract tests before migrating it; the package split must not redesign variant semantics.
- **Browser targets:** Latest stable Chromium-based browsers and latest stable Safari/WebKit on macOS/iOS; ignore Firefox. Verify required CSS and platform behavior on both engines with stock shipping features and recorded versions. No legacy-browser or Firefox polyfill requirement. If a chosen CSS mechanism fails on a target engine, find another implementation or revisit an explicit design/support decision; do not silently drop WebKit, change adaptive weights, freeze colors, or restore JavaScript generators.
- **Generator-owned assignment scope:** Variable generator descriptors declare `scope: 'shared' | 'contextual'` as authoritative policy. Core preserves the metadata through composition and extension; family core derives per-family contracts and permissible value inputs from contextual descriptors. Apps choose family names, values, and selection, with no separate `vary` list. Shared variables remain runtime-updateable but have one assignment across families; static descriptors are neither contextual nor runtime-updateable. This is a deliberate design-system policy, not an intrinsic limitation of a generator, and is independent of light/dark behavior.
- **Generator-owned output kind:** Static versus variable is an intrinsic immutable generator declaration, not a theme-composition decorator. Breakpoints always yield static queries; palette/background/grid generators always yield variable source/formula definitions, even when defaults are supplied. Core derives public output and legal setup/update inputs from that discriminant, preserves actual static types, and excludes static outputs from value assignment, family allocation, and editing. Nested theme groups compose self-describing descriptors directly; no consumer reclassification API.
- **Convenience contract returns:** Build-time and runtime setup calls, including family setup, return the existing public contract being rendered. Direct setup returns its theme; setup for an extended theme returns that extended contract. Rendering never creates or extends a contract, and family selection does not replace the returned public contract with family-specific references.
- **One-time generators and CSS dependencies:** Compile structure, bindings, and expressions once. Updates never rerun generators or compute derived colors/spacing in JavaScript. Relative colors and `calc(...)` react to sources; namespaces bind the compiled graph generically, with structural options fixed. Static generation is definition-time only. Contrast uses the selected native function and background mixing retains CSS-driven adaptive branches; no frozen initial decisions or runtime JavaScript fallback.
- **Native contrast with adaptive surface levels:** Use `contrast-color()` for derived black/white foregrounds, accepting native algorithm/tie semantics rather than the prior JavaScript WCAG choice. Keep surface/elevated/raised text-mix weights at 10/20/30% for light polarity and 20/40/50% for dark polarity; depressed/recessed mix toward the opposite color at 20/30% in either case. Polarity is input-derived, independent of light/dark selection. CSS conditionals and any private typed markers must stay reactive at the allocation root and be correctly namespaced/inheritable. Browser support and exact conditional mechanics still require verification; fixed percentages and generator reruns are not fallback policies.
- **Multiplicative Fibonacci spacing:** Use ratio sequence `2, 3, 5, 8, ...` around the main source: small = base / ratio, large = base * ratio. Keep existing token-path conventions (`m`, `s/l`, `xs/xl`, etc.); structural pair count is definition-time only. Emit fixed `calc(...)` coefficients rather than recomputing pairs on updates. Positive base values yield positive spacing; larger scales no longer subtract Fibonacci offsets into negatives. Existing Fibonacci values intentionally change, while the default eight-point generator remains unchanged.
- **One stylesheet renderer and current-content authority:** The shared backend handles static/SSR emission, browser adoption, and source updates. Current owned contents supply live values to the app and devtools; synchronize serialized text after CSSOM patches and expose current snapshots. Preserve rules, layers, nonces, ownership, SSR values, and Storybook mirroring. No separate mutable input cache, devtools override layer, or manifest value snapshot. Initial CSS precedes first paint; React wrappers and optional manifests are not runtime prerequisites.
- **Independent Vanilla-Extract-compatible contracts:** Remove Vanilla Extract production, peer, and exported-type dependencies from all theme layers and the renderer. Own deterministic valid/collision-checked variable names and precise plain nested `var(--...)` references while preserving existing public names and identity. Keep descriptors/editor metadata outside the variable contract and static tokens outside whole-contract variable projections. Vanilla Extract remains in component/page/styling consumers, which can use these structurally compatible references without an adapter. Verify compatibility in consumer tooling rather than introducing a production dependency.
- **Immutable contract namespaces:** Select a validated prefix at creation/binding, defaulting to `theme`; devtools uses `devtools-theme`. Namespace every owned public/private source/derived allocation, dependency, alias, family/variant name, and any property registration. Reuse compiled definitions to create another independent view without mutating the original or rerunning generators. Extension preserves its base namespace and identity. Preserve default public app names and remove unprefixed private collision paths. Consumers use the bound view appropriate to their namespace; no automatic app/devtools alias bridge.
- **Shadow-host UI isolation:** Private devtools sources/formulas live on its host through an inner shadow sheet targeting `:host`; widgets inherit those namespaced values. Mutable UI sheets are per instance; immutable structural sheets may be shared per document/namespace. Control typography, units, color-scheme, and CSP explicitly. These sheets are never inspected by devtools. Manifest ownership addresses application light-DOM allocations only; general renderer root/host support is not inspection permission.
- **Breakpoint boundary semantics and CSS syntax:** Retain `lt`, `gt`, `lte`, and `gte` for each named breakpoint. Emit `(width < Xpx)` for `lt`, `(width > Xpx)` for `gt`, `(max-width: Xpx)` for `lte`, and `(min-width: Xpx)` for `gte`. Emit `(Xpx < width < Ypx)` for `between`, excluding both endpoints. Do not subtract pixels or an epsilon to approximate strict comparisons; fractional widths must behave exactly.
- **Ordered breakpoint definitions:** Accept an ordered tuple of `[name, threshold]` entries instead of an object mapping. Require strictly increasing numeric thresholds and verify that order at construction; reject equal or descending thresholds. Generate `between` queries for every forward pair, including nonadjacent entries, but never reversed or same-endpoint pairs. Derive permissible range keys from tuple positions rather than type-level numeric arithmetic; runtime ordering validation keeps that positional model consistent with the numeric values.
- **Accurate breakpoint types:** Preserve names and numeric literals with a `const` generic for inline tuple definitions; separately declared definitions must retain their literals with `as const` or an equivalent declaration. Each output property has the exact emitted query string as its type. Derive `between` keys and endpoint literals from forward tuple pairs, so impossible range keys are absent at compile time as well as runtime. Widened numeric inputs cannot recover exact literals and must yield correspondingly widened query string types. Arbitrary query-intersection analysis is not part of this API.
- **Independent family value sets:** Treat every family, including `base`, as a separate theme with the same public tokens and independent contextual values. Missing contextual inputs use that family's own defaults, not another family member's values. Updating one family's contextual values never propagates to another family. Shared-scope variables remain a separate theme-wide assignment by descriptor policy; they are not inherited from `base`.
- **Explicit family value containers:** Family setup, updates, and live export use `{ shared, families }`. Shared-scope source paths belong in `shared`; each member's contextual paths belong in `families.<name>`, including ordinary `base`. Metadata determines legal placement, with no inheritance from other members and no configuration/family-key collisions. Missing setup inputs use local defaults; partial updates retain omitted current values. Direct setup remains unwrapped, and static/derived values never enter source inputs.
- **Clean cutover:** Migrate all affected consumers and package dependencies directly to the new owners, document the breaking API changes, and remove obsolete exports and implementation paths. Do not retain or introduce backwards-compatibility aliases, forwarding re-exports, legacy input adapters, or a staged compatibility layer.
- **Partial runtime updates:** Omitted paths retain current owned source allocations. The light/dark adapter supports partial variant inputs: a dark-only update preserves the current light input, including after scalar shorthand; a scalar writes both variants. Setup resolves complete inputs from local defaults plus supplied values, with missing required inputs without defaults rejected. Updates patch sources read through sheet bindings/codecs, never reset omissions to defaults or borrow another family's values. Other generator inputs are complete replacements unless their descriptor explicitly supports patches; no arbitrary generic `DeepPartial`. Types mirror supported patches, and no separate normalized-input cache or generator re-execution is needed.
- **Input-only devtools editing and live setup export:** Editors change source inputs such as a palette's main color, never individual derived outputs such as muted or emphasis. Discover manifest-enabled themes and family configurations, including inactive members of a declared family configuration, on build-time/SSR pages without theme runtime initialization as well as runtime-rendered pages. Export only live inputs as copyable setup-compatible values, preserving types and nested structure without exporting generated tokens; copying original setup values is not required.
- **Optional manifests and programmatic-first access:** Manifests are optional, JSON-safe inspection metadata derived from descriptors/root bindings, never a competing values store. Core initialization accepts manifests and React receives them as props; when not programmatically provided, devtools discovers designated embedded HTML/DOM manifests. Provided catalogs are authoritative and not implicitly merged with DOM data. No available manifest entry means no access, even if CSS is visible. Both paths use the same schema and permit SSR pages without theme runtime setup; normal rendering/update depends on neither. Empty-list/omission semantics are specified in the recommended precedence above, with exact schema/helper APIs still to settle.
- **Root-only, light-DOM devtools:** Read/edit declared application root sources in owned light-DOM sheets, for standard themes and all allocated families/variants. Exclude all Web Component shadow-root sheets and the private devtools UI theme, irrespective of shadow mode or metadata delivery path. No DOM picker, arbitrary element overrides, shadow traversal, or closed-root bridge. Descendant family selection consumes root values but is not an editable scope. Export live root inputs only.
- **Two devtools packages and Web Components UI:** Framework-agnostic core owns Web Components, shadow-root editors, handwritten CSS in TypeScript string modules, manifest resolution, and inspection/update/export. React hosts/binds to that core without another UI or value store. No Vanilla Extract extraction or bundler is needed for the devtools build. Its private theme uses independent defaults and a dedicated allocation host; nested widgets inherit its tokens. Imports/registration are SSR-safe, and disposal removes private UI resources but never resets inspected application allocations.
- **Devtools manifest delivery:** Primary delivery is an optional programmatic manifest list passed to the core initializer or React props. HTML/DOM discovery is used only when that input is absent, not as a supplement to a supplied list. The DOM mount point controls UI placement, not allocation ownership or access scope. Programmatic-only use does not implicitly emit a DOM catalog; optional embedding remains the path for independently discovered manifests, including a future Chrome frontend.

For an ordered definition of `mobile: 700`, `tablet: 1000`, and `screen: 1600`, the emitted values and their literal types include:

| Key | Emitted value and literal type |
| --- | --- |
| `lt-mobile` | `(width < 700px)` |
| `gt-mobile` | `(width > 700px)` |
| `lte-mobile` | `(max-width: 700px)` |
| `gte-mobile` | `(min-width: 700px)` |
| `between-mobile-tablet` | `(700px < width < 1000px)` |
| `between-mobile-screen` | `(700px < width < 1600px)` |
| `between-tablet-screen` | `(1000px < width < 1600px)` |

`between-tablet-mobile` and `between-mobile-mobile` are not keys of the result. Individual `lt-mobile` and `gt-tablet` queries remain valid; their impossible intersection is not a generated `between` query.

## Remaining design details and semantic decisions

- The manifest/editor wire schema, declarative codecs, and programmatic initialization/React-prop/DOM-embedding helpers. Numeric units and supported structured inputs must round-trip to live setup values; do not embed executable functions or infer original inputs from derived output. Programmatic-first and DOM-fallback delivery are settled; recommended exact empty-list and invalid-input semantics are documented above.
- Exact stylesheet ownership/allocation IDs, server isolation, SSR adoption, duplicate policy, and safe nonce/serialization APIs. Devtools manifest addressing only needs application roots and owned sheets in light DOM; shadow inspection/open-versus-closed access is not an outstanding product choice. The renderer still needs document/shadow contexts for private UI rendering, with independent mutable sheets and shared immutable structural styles. Chrome's later cross-context transport preserves the same light-DOM target scope.
- The exact CSS implementation and capability checks for native contrast/adaptive percentages on latest stable Chromium and Safari/WebKit. `if()` is experimental in current documentation, so verify it or an equivalent CSS path on both target engines without assuming Chromium success establishes Safari support. Cover computed foreground conditions, typed/private registration, transparency/wide gamut, and document/shadow contexts. Browser targets and color policies are settled; an unsupported target requires a verified alternative or explicit design decision, not silent engine exclusion or forbidden value fallbacks.
- Supported editor kinds, patch validation, notifications, catalog replacement/DOM refresh, custom-element registration/version conflicts, hot-reload reconciliation, supported browser/CSP behavior, and UI inheritance/units. Keep schemas generic and core framework-independent. UI mounting, private UI theme roots, and inspected roots are distinct; Chrome's cross-context connection remains a future concern.
- Reset/restore semantics if a reset control is included. Application and devtools writes share the source-update path; separate override layers, initial-value copying, persistence, and undo/history are not requirements.
